questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘SOLID’ is coded as ‘64’ and ‘POUR’ IS coded as ‘74’ How will ‘TON’ be coded as in that language?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain code language, ‘SOLID’ is coded as ‘64’ and ‘POUR’ IS coded as ‘74’ How will ‘TON’ be coded as in that language?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is,

For SOLID,

The place value of S is 19

The place value of O is 15

The place value of L is 12

The place value of I is 9

The place value of D is 4

SOLID → 19 + 15 + 12 + 9 + 4 = 59

59 + 5 = 64( we added 5 because there are 5 letters in SOLID)

SOLID is coded as 64

For POUR,

The place value of P is 16

The place value of O is 15

The place value of U is 21

The place value of R is 18

POUR → 16 + 15 + 21 + 18 = 70

70 + 4 = 74( we added 4 because there are 4 letters in POUR)

POUR is coded as 74

Similarly,

For TON,

The place value of T is 20

The place value of O is 15

The place value of N is 14

TON → 20 + 15 + 14 = 49

49 + 3 = 52

TON is coded as 52

Hence, “52” is the correct answer.

questions.question: A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as _____.
questions.questionHtml: A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as _____.
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, i.e. Deficit Financing.

Key Points

  • A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as Deficit Financing. 
  • In the case of Deficit Financing, the government has to either borrow or look for other means to cover the expenditure.
  • As per the National Planning Commission of India, ‘deficit financing’ term is used to denote the direct addition to gross national expenditure through budget deficits.
  • The deficits can be met by raising the rates of taxation. It can also be done by increasing the price of public utility services.
  • There can be many deficits- Budget deficit, Revenue deficit, Fiscal Deficit, Monetized Fiscal Deficit, etc.

questions.solution:
Formula Used:

\(\frac{{M1.D1.T1.E1}}{{W1.C1}} = \;\frac{{M2.D2.T2.E2}}{{W2.C2}}\)

M is the number of working men

D is the total number of days

T is total hours of working days

E is the efficiency of working men

W is total work

C is the consumption of working men

Calculation:

187 men worked for 65 days working 15 hours per day

And completed 3/5 of the work.

Remaining work,

⇒ 1 – 3/5 = 2/5

Now using the formula,

Let the total men required to complete the job be x.

M1 × D1 × H1/W1 = M2 × D2 × H2/W2

⇒(187 × 65 × 15)/(3/5) = (x × 10 × 17]/(2/5)

⇒ x = 11 × 65

⇒ x = 715

Additional men,

⇒ 715 – 187 = 528 men

∴ Additional man to be employed is 528.
